- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract pessimism bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and model forecast is below recent 5-day average, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with bullish sentiment.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply a 0.8–1.2% upward bias for first 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag mean reversion; add 0.3–0.7% upward adjustment for days with mixed sentiment.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if model consistently underestimates by 0.5–1.0% relative to 10-day moving average, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward correction to align with trend persistence.
